arxiv-1908-11146.title: Towards More Usable Dataset Search: From Query Characterization to Snippet Generation Conference: The 28th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management; November 3–7, 2019; Beijing, China The 28th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM ’19)
arxiv-1908-11146.creator: Jinchi Chen, Xiaxia Wang, Gong Cheng, Evgeny Kharlamov, Yuzhong Qu
arxiv-1908-11146.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Jinchi Chen, Xiaxia Wang, Gong Cheng, Evgeny Kharlamov, Yuzhong Qu. Reusing published datasets on the Web is of great interest to researchers and developers. Their data needs may be met by submitting queries to a dataset search engine to retrieve relevant datasets. In this ongoing work towards developing a more usable dataset search engine, we characterize real data needs by annotating the semantics of 1,947 queries using a novel fine-grained scheme, to provide implications for enhancing dataset search.

arxiv-2207-10979.title: Cryptanalysis of a System based on Twisted Dihedral Group Algebras
arxiv-2207-10979.creator: Simran Tinani
arxiv-2207-10979.description: Abstract Several cryptographic protocols constructed based on less-known algorithmic problems, such as those in non-commutative groups, group rings, semigroups, etc., which claim quantum security, have been broken through classical reduction methods within their specific proposed platforms. A rigorous examination of the complexity of these algorithmic problems is therefore an important topic of research.

arxiv-2301-06056.title: Improving Noise Robustness for Spoken Content Retrieval using semi-supervised ASR and N-best transcripts for BERT-based ranking models
arxiv-2301-06056.creator: Yasufumi Moriya, Gareth. J. F. Jones
arxiv-2301-06056.description: Abstract BERT-based re-ranking and dense retrieval (DR) systems have been shown to improve search effectiveness for spoken content retrieval (SCR). However, both methods can still show a reduction in effectiveness when using ASR transcripts in comparison to accurate manual transcripts.

arxiv-2312-00894.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Improve REST API Testing Conference: New Ideas and Emerging Results ; April 14–20, 2024; Lisbon, Portugal New Ideas and Emerging Results (ICSE-NIER’24), April 14–20, 2024, Lisbon, Portugal DOI: 10.1145/3639476.3639769 ISBN: 979-8-4007-0500-7/24/04 CCS: Information
arxiv-2312-00894.creator: Myeongsoo Kim, Tyler Stennett, Dhruv Shah, Saurabh Sinha, Alessandro Orso
arxiv-2312-00894.description: Abstract . The widespread adoption of REST APIs, coupled with their growing complexity and size, has led to the need for automated REST API testing tools. Current tools focus on the structured data in REST API specifications but often neglect valuable insights available in unstructured natural-language descriptions in the specifications, which leads to suboptimal test coverage.

arxiv-2402-15258.title: High Resolution Guitar Transcription via Domain Adaptation
arxiv-2402-15258.creator: Xavier Riley*, Drew Edwards*, Simon Dixon
arxiv-2402-15258.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Xavier Riley*, Drew Edwards*, Simon Dixon. Automatic music transcription (AMT) has achieved high accuracy for piano due to the availability of large, high-quality datasets such as MAESTRO and MAPS, but comparable datasets are not yet available for other instruments. In recent work, however, it has been demonstrated that aligning scores to transcription model activations can produce high quality AMT training data for instruments other than piano.

arxiv-2403-04855.title: MINDS: JWST/NIRCam imaging of the protoplanetary disk PDS 70
arxiv-2403-04855.creator: V. Christiaens, M. Samland, Th. Henning, B. Portilla-Revelo, G. Perotti, E. Matthews, O. Absil, L. Decin, I. Kamp, A. Boccaletti, B. Tabone, G.-D. Marleau, E. F. van Dishoeck, M. Güdel, P.-O. Lagage, D. Barrado, A. Caratti o Garatti, A. M. Glauser, G. Olofsson, T. P. Ray, S. Scheithauer, B. Vandenbu
arxiv-2403-04855.description: Abstract Context. Two protoplanets have recently been discovered within the PDS 70 protoplanetary disk. JWST/NIRCam offers a unique opportunity to characterize them and their birth environment at wavelengths that are difficult to access from the ground. Aims. We image the circumstellar environment of PDS 70 at 1.87 μ \upmu m and 4.

arxiv-2409-06402.title: Symmetry Breaking in Neural Network Optimization: Insights from Input Dimension Expansion
arxiv-2409-06402.creator: Jun-Jie Zhang, Nan Cheng, Fu-Peng Li, Xiu-Cheng Wang, Jian-Nan Chen, Long-Gang Pang, Deyu Meng
arxiv-2409-06402.description: Abstract Understanding the mechanisms behind neural network optimization is crucial for improving network design and performance. While various optimization techniques have been developed, a comprehensive understanding of the underlying principles that govern these techniques remains elusive. Specifically, the role of symmetry breaking, a fundamental concept in physics, has not been fully explored in neural network optimization.

arxiv-2503-15636.title: A computational approach to rational summability and its applications via discrete residues
arxiv-2503-15636.creator: Carlos E. Arreche, Hari P. Sitaula
arxiv-2503-15636.description: Abstract . A rational function f ⁡ ( x ) f(x) is rationally summable if there exists a rational function g ⁡ ( x ) g(x) such that f ⁡ ( x ) = g ⁡ ( x + 1 ) − g ⁡ ( x ) f(x)=g(x+1)-g(x) .

arxiv-2505-21400.title: Breaking AR’s Sampling Bottleneck: Provable Acceleration via Diffusion Language Models 0 0 footnotetext: The authors contributed equally. Corresponding author: Changxiao Cai.
arxiv-2505-21400.creator: Gen Li, Changxiao Cai
arxiv-2505-21400.description: Abstract Diffusion models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for modern generative modeling, demonstrating strong potential for large language models (LLMs). Unlike conventional autoregressive (AR) models that generate tokens sequentially, diffusion models allow for parallel sampling, offering a promising path to accelerate generation and eliminate the left-to-right generation constraints.

arxiv-2506-02303.title: A Bayesian Spatio-Temporal Top-Down Framework for Estimating Opioid Use Disorder Risk Under Data Sparsity
arxiv-2506-02303.creator: Emily N. Peterson, Alex A. Edwards, Martha Wetzel, Lance A. Waller, Hannah Cooper, Courtney Yarbrough
arxiv-2506-02303.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Emily N. Peterson, Alex A. Edwards, Martha Wetzel, Lance A. Waller, Hannah Cooper, Courtney Yarbrough. County-level estimates of opioid use disorder (OUD) are essential for understanding the influence of local economic and social conditions. They provide policymakers with the granular information needed to identify, target, and implement effective interventions and allocate resources appropriately. Traditional disease mapping methods typically rely on Poisson regression, modeling observed counts while adjusting for local covariates that are treated as fixed and known.

arxiv-2511-00110.title: Chain of Time: In-Context Physical Simulation with Image Generation Models
arxiv-2511-00110.creator: YingQiao Wang, Eric Bigelow, Boyi Li, Tomer Ullman
arxiv-2511-00110.description: Abstract We propose a novel cognitively-inspired method to improve and interpret physical simulation in vision-language models. Our “Chain of Time” method involves generating a series of intermediate images during a simulation, and it is motivated by in-context reasoning in machine learning, as well as mental simulation in humans.

arxiv-2601-01258.title: On the local anisotropy of quasi-two-dimensional forced shallow flow: an experimental study
arxiv-2601-01258.creator: Ghassan Antar 1 , Jamal El Kuweiss 1 , Kai Schneider 2 , Charbel Habchi 3 and Sadruddin Benkadda 4
arxiv-2601-01258.description: Abstract We experimentally investigate quasi-two-dimensional (Q2D) forced shallow flows in the presence of solid boundaries and analyze the deviation from the Kolmogorov-Kraichnan (KK) theory. Complex motion is generated using a thin electrolyte subject to electromagnetic forces, and we employ particle tracking velocimetry to resolve the flow properties down to the Kolmogorov scale.

plos-pone-0006209.creator: Glen M. DeLoid, Timothy H. Sulahian, Amy Imrich et al.
plos-pone-0006209.description: PLOS ONE research article. Alveolar macrophages (AMs) can phagocytose unopsonized pathogens such as S. aureus via innate immune receptors, such as scavenger receptors (SRs). Cytoskeletal events and signaling pathways involved in phagocytosis of unopsonized bacteria likely govern the fate of ingested pathog

plos-pone-0356205.title: Nintedanib in the prevention of radiation-induced lung injury in patients with unresectable stage II-III NSCLC: A protocol for a randomized, multicenter, control group study
plos-pone-0356205.creator: Ai Cui, Anhui Shi, Lei Deng, Yanyan Sun, Jiayi Yu, Xinrong Lian, Ziyue Zhao
plos-pone-0356205.description: Nintedanib in the prevention of radiation-induced lung injury in patients with unresectable stage II-III NSCLC: A protocol for a randomized, multicenter, control group study

pmc-10520453.title: Global quantitative understanding of non-equilibrium cell fate decision-making in response to pheromone
pmc-10520453.creator: Sheng Li, Qiong Liu, Erkang Wang, Jin Wang
pmc-10520453.description: SummaryCell-cycle arrest and polarized growth are commonly used to characterize the response of yeast to pheromone. However, the quantitative decision-making processes underlying time-dependent changes in cell fate remain unclear. In this study, we conducted single-cell level experiments to observe multidimensional responses, uncovering diverse fates of yeast cells.

pmc-10692761.title: Structome: a tool for the rapid assembly of datasets for structural phylogenetics
pmc-10692761.creator: Ashar J Malik, Desiree Langer, Chandra S Verma, Anthony M Poole, Jane R Allison, Alex Bateman
pmc-10692761.description: SummaryProtein structures carry signal of common ancestry and can therefore aid in reconstructing their evolutionary histories. To expedite the structure-informed inference process, a web server, Structome, has been developed that allows users to rapidly identify protein structures similar to a query protein and to assemble datasets useful for structure-based phylogenetics.

pmc-10737554.title: THE IMPACT OF CONTRACT NURSE UTILIZATION ON NURSING HOME QUALITY
pmc-10737554.creator: Ganisher Davlyatov, Robert Weech-Maldonado, Rohit Pradhan, Akbar Ghiasi, Justin Lord
pmc-10737554.description: Nurse staffing intensity and skill mix have a significant impact on NH quality of care. For instance, higher staffing levels, particularly for registered nurses (RNs), have been associated with better resident outcomes. NHs have increasingly relied on contract nurse staffing to address pressing and persistent nursing shortages.

pmc-11462053.title: Using machine learning to predict the risk of developing hypertensive disorders of pregnancy using a contemporary nulliparous cohort
pmc-11462053.creator: Jonathan S. Schor, Adesh Kadambi, Isabel Fulcher, Kartik K. Venkatesh, Mark A. Clapp, Senan Ebrahim, Ali Ebrahim, Timothy Wen
pmc-11462053.description: BackgroundHypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are significant drivers of maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality. Current management strategies include early identification and initiation of risk mitigating interventions facilitated by a rules-based checklist. Advanced analytic techniques, such as machine learning, can potentially offer improved and refined predictive capabilities.

pmc-11472074.title: Development, assessment and validation of a novel nomogram model for predicting stroke mimics in stroke center：A single-center observational study
pmc-11472074.creator: Xiaoman Chen, Shuo Zhang
pmc-11472074.description: BackgroundEarly recognition and prediction of stroke mimics (SM) can avoid inappropriate recanalization therapy and delay in the management of SM etiology. The purpose of this study is to screen the predictors for SM and develop a novel predictive nomogram model for predicting SM. Meanwhile, the diagnostic performance of the nomogram model was evaluated and validated.

pmc-11677383.title: Biological Properties and Phytochemicals of Multipurpose Tree Plant Hagenia abyssinica
pmc-11677383.creator: Varun Jaiswal, Hae-Jeung Lee
pmc-11677383.description: Hagenia abyssinica (HA) is a monotypic tree species used as traditional medicine against various diseases and conditions in African countries. HA is also a multipurpose plant used for furniture, fuel wood, soil fertility management, and rainwater conservation, along with medicinal usage.

pmc-12436833.title: The use of computer-aided analysis of facial expressions based on the support vector machine in the diagnosis of ASD
pmc-12436833.creator: K. Kania, K. Wilczyński, D. Pęszor, L. Cichoń, K. Wojciechowski, A. Kawalec, M. Janas-Kozik
pmc-12436833.description: IntroductionAutism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by communication challenges, particularly in non-verbal aspects such as facial expressions.Research in this area is limited due to the lack of accurate methodologies. Existing literature generally agrees that individuals with ASD often show a disconnect between verbal communication and emotional expression, with facial expressions being diminished or inappropriate.

pmc-12505847.title: A case of congenital total intestinal atresia in a neonate: a case report
pmc-12505847.creator: Hindeya Hailu Hagos, Yemane Leake Gebremichael, Birhanu Kassie Reta, Tiegist Bahta Woldu, Hailemariam Kahsay Kidanu, Gebreyohans Tesfay Kidanu
pmc-12505847.description: IntroductionIntestinal atresia is the complete occlusion of the intestinal lumen at various parts of the intestine. It has the potential to cause intestinal failure. Two mechanisms are suggested: failure of recanalization and/or accidental injury. This case report aims to discuss an exceptionally rare case of congenital total intestinal atresia.

pmc-12722019.title: Identification the Tumor Mechanics-Related Biomarkers in Gastric Cancer Patients Based on Bioinformatics and Machine Learning
pmc-12722019.creator: Minzhi Sun, Qing Liu, Aman Xu
pmc-12722019.description: BackgroundGastric cancer (GC) remains a major cause of cancer related mortality worldwide. Tumor mechanics, reflecting the physical and mechanical properties that influence tumor cell behavior and the tumor microenvironment (TME), play important roles in cancer progression. However, the prognostic relevance of tumor mechanics-related genes (MRGs) in GC remains unclear.

pmc-12788428.title: Toxic Dust: Measuring Awareness about Third-Hand Smoke Contamination in Homes Among Smokers and Non-smokers of Family Members—A Cross-sectional Study
pmc-12788428.creator: N Nagappan, T. Manigandan
pmc-12788428.description: Background:Third-hand smoke (THS) poses significant health risks through persistent toxic residues, yet awareness remains inadequate, particularly in high-smoking populations like India. This study assessed THS knowledge gaps between smokers and non-smokers in Chennai households.Methods:A community-based cross-sectional study surveyed 450 adults (225 smokers, 225 non-smokers) using multistage cluster sampling. A validated 20-item questionnaire measured THS knowledge, attitudes, and practices.

pmc-13411703.title: Humanization of Surgical Care in the Robotic Age: A Triangular Interaction Model Between the Surgeon, the Patient, and the Technology
pmc-13411703.creator: Giuseppe Zimmitti, Maria Rosaria Portinaio, Alessandro Morandi, Paolo Terzi, Angelo Meloni, Luca Lavazza, Maria Clotilde Carra, Cinzia Ravaioli, Nicola de’Angelis
pmc-13411703.description: Background/Objectives: In modern medicine, humanization of care is a central theme that highlights the complementarity of clinical care with empathy, communication, and patient-centered values. The increasing use of robotic surgery is rapidly modifying surgical practice, introducing new challenges and opportunities in preserving the human dimension of care.

pmc-13428710.title: Anxiety disorders: a cross-sectional study of clinical and biological associations
pmc-13428710.creator: Jessica L Fernandes, Graziela Amboni, Camila O Arent, Lucas C Pedro, Gabriel S Mondo, Flavia S Niero, Josimar G Pereira, Margarete D Bagatini, Zuleide Maria Ignácio, Luciane B Ceretta, Gislaine Z Réus

pmc-13477035.title: On the ancestry and evolution of the extinct dire wolf
pmc-13477035.creator: Gregory L Gedman, Kathleen Morrill Pirovich, Jonas Oppenheimer, Chaz Hyseni, Molly Cassatt-Johnstone, Alexander G Lucaci, Nicolas Alexandre, William Troy, J Chris Chao, Olivier Fedrigo, Savannah J Hoyt, Patrick GS Grady, Sam Sacco, William Seligmann, Ayusman Dash, Mithil Chokshi, Laura Knecht, James B Papizan, Tyler Miyawaki, Sven Bocklandt, James Kelher, Sara Ord, Shyam Gopalakrishnan, Audrey T Lin, Brandon R Peecook, Angela Perri, Mikkel-Holger S Sinding, Greger Larson, Julie Meachen, Love Dalén, Bridgett vonHoldt, M Thomas P Gilbert, Christopher E Mason, Rachel J O'Neill, Elinor K Karlsson, Brandi L Cantarel, George RR Martin, George Church, Ben Lamm, Beth Shapiro

pmc-13602833.title: Incidental Detection of a Right-to-Left Atrial Shunt Without Pulmonary Hypertension
pmc-13602833.creator: Shiv Malhotra, Calista Kee, Leeza Peerzada, William M Strub
pmc-13602833.description: Right-to-left interatrial shunting permits venous blood to bypass the pulmonary circulation and enter the systemic circulation, potentially contributing to hypoxemia and paradoxical embolization. Although sustained right-to-left shunting is commonly associated with elevated right-sided or pulmonary arterial pressures, it may also occur in patients with normal pulmonary pressures because of transient pressure gradients or preferential flow across an interatrial communication.

pmc-13605955.title: Efficacy and Safety of Immunotherapeutic Strategies for the Treatment of MART-1-Expressing Melanoma: Systematic Review of Clinical Trials
pmc-13605955.creator: Alina Alshevskaya, Sofya Tsarikova, Elena Golikova, Peter Timashev, Sergey Sennikov
pmc-13605955.description: Simple SummaryImmunotherapy has become an important treatment strategy for patients with advanced melanoma. Melanoma antigen recognized by T cells 1 (MART-1) has been extensively investigated as a target for a variety of immunotherapeutic approaches, including DNA- and peptide-based vaccines, adoptive cell therapies, and combination strategies. However, the clinical efficacy and safety of these approaches have not been systematically compared.

pmc-13642936.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor activation and mental health: a drug-target mendelian randomization study
pmc-13642936.creator: Guoyi Yang, Stephen Burgess, C Mary Schooling
pmc-13642936.description: Concerns have been raised about the psychiatric safety of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists, but trial evidence suggests that they ameliorate depressive symptoms. We aimed to assess the associations of GLP-1R activation with mental health well-being and the risk of mental health disorders and substance use disorders.

pmc-13674458.title: Probiotics‐derived postbiotics improve host metabolic syndrome by activating the adipocyte thermogenic signaling pathway in high‐fat diet‐fed mice
pmc-13674458.creator: Ye Tian, Liujing Huang, Yifan Liu, Xudong Mai, Yanbo Cheng, Bingdong Liu, Yixin Chen, Liwei Xie
pmc-13674458.description: Metabolic syndrome, including type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, represents a global health challenge. While probiotics can modulate host metabolism, postbiotics (inanimate microbial preparations) have emerged as potentially safer and more stable therapeutic alternatives. The current study investigates the effects of postbiotics derived from five human‐origin bacterial strains in mice model with high‐fat diet‐induced metabolic syndrome.

uslaw-usc-t42-s2002.title: 42 U.S.C. § 2002 — Transfer of hospitals and facilities to State or private institutions; conditions and restrictions; failure to meet requirements
uslaw-usc-t42-s2002.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s2002.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 22 (Indian Hospitals And Health Facilities); Subchapter I (Maintenance And Operation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whenever the health needs of the Indians can be better met thereby, the Secretary of Health and Human Services is authorized in his discretion to enter into contracts with any State, Territory, or political subdivision.
